biggestGap: Make the gold and violet fills brighten ALONG THEIR LENGTH, not just across their thickness. Right now --grad-gold-metal in primitives.css is 180deg only, so .bar__fill has a dead-flat body: measured on the list's 98.3% Sunforging XP bar at y=881, luma reads 164.0 163.9 164.0 163.9 164.0 163.2 164.0 163.0 162.2 163.9 164.0 163.2 164.0 163.9 164.0 across 375px (188 CSS px) — total variation under 2 luma — and then jumps to the 242 cap. The reference does the opposite at EVERY bar size: its 65.4% XP bar runs 142 -> 148 -> 157 -> 164 -> 172 -> 177 -> 186 -> 200 -> 214 before its 247 cap; its small 78% QUEST bar runs 137.5 -> 198.2; its 92% UPGRADE violet runs 77.7 -> 97.3. End/start is ~1.45-1.50x for gold and ~1.25x for violet, always measured across the bar's own fill, so the sheen stretches as the fill grows. Add a 90deg component to the fill background (keep the 180deg cross-section, which is already correct) taking gold from ~L135 at the fill's left to ~L205 at its leading edge and violet from ~L72 to ~L92. This also fixes the second half of the problem for free: our cap is 242 over a body of 164 = 1.48x, which is why it reads as a glowing bead bolted onto the end — the reference's cap is 247 over a pre-cap 214 = 1.15x, a crest on a climb. Ramp the body to 205 and the existing 242 cap becomes 1.18x and stops looking like a sprite. Ten bars carry that bead in the list view today, which turns one effect into wallpaper.

MATH IS EXACT, 22/22 ROWS, ZERO DRIFT, ALL THE WAY TO 120. Ran src/js/engine/xp.js against every row in reference/melvor-math.md, cumulative AND per-step: L1..L10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 92, 99, 110, 120. Every single delta 0, including 13,034,431 / 1,228,825 at 99 and 104,273,167 / 9,830,430 at 120. doublingRatio 10/30/66/92 = 1.9946 / 1.9955 / 1.9997 / 2.0000, matching the doc's '1.995 by 10, exactly 2.000 by 66'. The screen is bound to that table and not to constants: it showed '774 / 7,887 XP' and deltaXp(48) computes to 7887; 'TOTAL XP 75.9K' = xpAt(47) 75,127 + 774 = 75,901. ROUND 1'S NAMED GAP IS GENUINELY CLOSED, AND I RE-MEASURED IT RATHER THAN TAKING THE BUILD RECORD'S WORD. Track cross-section, ours vs reference, same units: top rim 63.3 vs 62.4, bottom rim 54.4 vs 52.8, interior 23.2 vs 23.2 — that is a match to within a luma point on all three bands. Fill cross-section: ours 222.6 -> 145.4 with a lift back to 172.7 on the last two rows; the reference 213.1 -> 144.7 with a lift to 155.6, 166.8. The lit bottom edge is real and correct. Cap and bloom: ours peaks 242 and decays 81.9, 78.9, 75.4, 70.4, 66.6, 61.7 ... 23.2; the reference peaks 246.7 and decays 197, 125, 109, 85, 74, 63 ... 25. Seams are lit now, not cut. This is the round-1 critique executed at the pixel level.

BLIND A/B, LABELS STRIPPED — THE REFERENCE STILL READS AS THE SHIPPED PRODUCT, AND THE TELL IS MATERIAL, NOT LAYOUT. Cropped three matched bands at equal CSS scale (progress/shots/skill-loop-r2-critic-ab-*.png). Panel band: ours is close enough that I had to measure rather than look — same groove polarity, same track rims, same white/secondary split. Bar band: the reference's little QUEST/UPGRADE bars visibly climb toward their ends; ours sit flat with a bright dot. Nav band: the reference's five icons are modelled objects — a gold shield with a beveled crest and a rim glow, a steel helm with speculars, a faceted diamond with internal facet lines, a violet portal with a glowing eye — four or more values each. Ours are two-value silhouettes: a plain house, a plain skull, a plain diamond, an oval. Only the active anvil carries gold. That band alone gives the blind test away.

THE TOP 186 CSS PX IS THE EMPTIEST REGION ON THE SCREEN. The title block itself is a faithful reproduction of the reference's — emblem, letter-spaced gold serif label, giant gradient numeral, violet rarity word, thin rule interrupted by a diamond ornament, status line with a gold dot — and the ornament is a genuine micro-detail win. But it sits on a flat violet radial (centre sampled #1A0E41, luma 20.2 at the crown, falling to the #050A10 ground by y=360) carrying one 12 CSS px sprite, where the reference fills the same proportion of screen with painted art at luma 55-120. The list view repeats it at the other end: ~65 CSS px of dead ground between the last skill row and the nav.

THE LEVEL-UP MOMENT IS REAL BUT BADLY STAGED. The plate is the best piece of metal in the project — chamfered, framed, a proper face gradient with a lit bottom edge and near-black engraved serif. It lands at 87% down the screen, on top of the mastery pool panel, where its scrim leaves the pool figures half-legible behind it ('2.25...' ghosted at the plate's top edge). It celebrates a level-up while occluding the two live readouts a player is watching, and it is nowhere near the level numeral that just changed.

THUMB TEST AND HYGIENE ALL PASS, INDEPENDENTLY MEASURED. Live at 390x844: #runBtn 44x44, #backBtn 85.5x44, .rrow 356x79.4, .srow 356x96, .nav__item 71.6x47 — every interactive element at or above the project's own --tap-min: 44px, and round 1's two failures are gone. document.scrollWidth == innerWidth == 390, no horizontal scroll. Off-grid audit over every element under main: 9 hits total, and they are 44px of header safe padding plus 5px/7px chip padding on .rrow__req — nothing structural. `npm run verify`: 20 passed, 0 failed, including 'no raw hex outside tokens.css'.

TYPOGRAPHY IS ON SPEC, THOUGH SET LARGER THAN THE REFERENCE. Every uppercase label is 11px at 0.1em in #C4C8CA at full strength — the doc's own numbers, and nothing is muted to illegibility. Measured optically against the reference: our 'SKILL PROGRESS' has a 16px cap height at DPR 2 (8.0 CSS px); the reference's 'PROGRESS TO NEXT LEVEL' has a 16px cap at DPR 2.585 (6.19 CSS px). Ours is 29% physically larger, so our panels are airier and less dense than the reference's, but per-character tracking normalised to cap height is actually TIGHTER than the reference's (0.66 vs 0.76). This is a density choice, not a craft error, and I am not calling it the gap.

WHAT I DID NOT TEST: real-device safe areas. base.css defines .safe-top/.safe-bottom off env(), but headless emulation reports 0 insets, so 'nothing under the safe areas' is unproven on hardware — the nav labels currently sit 16.5 CSS px off the bottom edge, which would land inside an iPhone home-indicator strip if the inset does not apply. Worth one check on a real handset before this piece is called done.
